structured_output.summary:
I couldn't find any public CIFAR-100 result faster than our E023 (6.65 s). The CIFAR-100 speedrun repo lists only the organizers' ResNet9 baseline (75.36% in 59.3 s). The futurebiohackers PR, which reported 75.29% in 8.11 s on an A100-SXM4, now returns 404. The most useful outside evidence is Fulcrum/Fable's CIFAR-10 record work, and it points to three directions.

1. **Biggest untested lever: per-step host overhead.** Fable runs the entire training run as one CUDA graph, with batches staged in persistent per-step buffers and the schedule read from a GPU table. That brings fixed per-step overhead down to about 0.2 ms, against 1.5–4 ms for a plain compiled loop. A 24 px step then costs 0.575x a 32 px step, close to the 0.5625 FLOP ratio. Ours costs 0.68x (E008), which suggests about 1–2 ms of overhead is still left per step. This supports H2.4, and it also changes the reading of the resize results (E013, E018). Fulcrum found that the 24/28/32 curriculum saves net time only when steps scale with FLOPs. With a plain compile it lost time.
2. **Constants worth retuning.** Fable's champion recipe uses:
   - an LR floor at 5% of peak;
   - a short EMA tail (lerp every 4 steps, decay 0.7, starting 8 steps before the decay ends);
   - label smoothing 0.09, translate 2, batch 1536 and fp16;
   - a whiten-bias phase of only 0.2 epochs;
   - Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized momentum on conv filters.

   The airbench96 constants we inherited were tuned for 37 epochs: whiten_bias_epochs 3, Lookahead every 5 steps with a cubic alpha ramp, 10% warmup starting at 0.2x, and decay to 0. Note also that the original airbench96 net is 128/384/512 with a residual over the last two convs per block, not 128/384/576.
3. **Ceiling and literature context.**
   - airbench96 reaches 79.27% on CIFAR-100 without cutout and 79.76% with it, at 37 epochs and with no retuning. So the architecture's ceiling is far above 75%.
   - The airbench paper finds that the epochs each feature saves add up roughly independently.
   - Weight averaging combined with LR annealing cut about 12% of GPU-hours in AlgoPerf.
   - On CIFAR-100, Muon and momentum-schedule gains are smaller than on CIFAR-10.

Caveats:
- Fable's numbers are from CIFAR-10 at 94%, a different regime from our under-fitting 100-class run.
- I couldn't re-check the futurebiohackers claim that Muon lost to SGD at every size.
- The official judging GPU (PCIe, 300 W) is slower than this SXM4 (400 W), so measured times won't carry over exactly.
- The Fable blog says precomputing augmentation off the clock is specification gaming. Under RULES it must stay in the timed prepare/train.

findings.claim: With a whole-run CUDA graph (Fable e1), a 24 px step costs 0.575x and a 28 px step 0.774x a 32 px step, near the FLOP-theory values of 0.562 and 0.766, with ~0.2 ms per-step overhead. With plain compile plus an eager _foreach optimizer and loader work between auto-graphed steps (e5), the overhead is ~1.5-4 ms/step: the 24 px step is charged at 0.82x (~0.65x steady state), and there is a ~0.6 s lazy-compile warm-up leak at the extra resolution. On e1, the 24->28->32 curriculum gave a net -0.081 s (1.903 -> 1.823 s at matched accuracy, n=200). It needed ~0.45 extra epochs to repay a -0.12 pp loss. On e5 the same move lost time.
findings.relevance: Our 24 px step costs ~0.68x (E008), close to Fulcrum's 'plain compile' regime. That suggests ~1-2 ms/step of non-FLOP overhead is still left, even after E022. Removing it would cut time directly and would also make every resize schedule pay better. This may explain why E013 and E018 sit on a flat ~0.4 pp/s line.

findings.claim: Fable's CIFAR-10 champion runs one mega CUDA graph for the whole run. Per-step scalars (3 SGD LRs, the ortho LR, the NS target magnitude) are precomputed into a GPU table that the graph reads, and batches come from persistent per-step buffers filled before replay. Flip uses a pre-flipped every-other-epoch scheme; translate (pad + batch_crop) and brightness/contrast jitter are compiled functions that run before the graph. The EMA/Lookahead is torch._foreach_lerp_ inside the graph.
findings.relevance: Concrete design for the next throughput step beyond E022: capture the whole run, not just the per-step graph, and stage augmentation into per-step buffers inside train/prepare. Under RULES this staging is timed, but it runs as large batched kernels rather than per-step launches.

Gives values to test for the open re-tune hypotheses. An LR floor of 5% plus a short EMA tail tests H4.5.1. Batch 1536 tests H4.4 and the 'test larger batches' contingency after E015. A 0.2-epoch whiten-bias phase, against our inherited 3 epochs, bears on H4.5. Muon-style ortho momentum on conv filters bears on H4.2.1. Translate 2 and LS ~0.1 agree with E011 and E014.

Confirms which constants were tuned for 37 epochs and still sit in our ~11-epoch recipe. whiten_bias_epochs 3 is ~27% of an 11-epoch run (Fable uses 0.2 of 8.9). The cubic Lookahead ramp and the 0.2x warmup start are also untested at this budget. The original block-3 width is 512, and blocks have a residual. Our 576/704 block 3 and the tree's 'airbench96 128/384/576' label should be checked against this layout.

findings.claim: airbench96 on CIFAR-100 with no hyperparameter retuning: 79.27% without cutout, 79.76% with cutout. CIFAR-10 epochs-to-94% in the ablations: whitening init 21 ep; + dirac 18 ep; + bias scaler (BN-bias LR) 13.5 ep; + Lookahead 12.0 ep; + multi-crop TTA 10.8 ep. Epochs saved by each feature (other than TTA) are similar whether the feature is added or removed, i.e. the speedups add up rather than multiply.
findings.relevance: The architecture's long-schedule ceiling is ~4 pp above the target. Cutout helps only at 37 epochs (+0.5 pp), consistent with H4.1.4 (regularization should scale with budget). Bias scaler and Lookahead are each worth 1.5-4.5 CIFAR-10 epochs, so their short-budget settings deserve re-tuning (H4.5). Because feature gains add up, small independent gains can be stacked.

findings.claim: airbench94_muon: widths 64/256/256, batch 2000, 8 epochs, whiten bias trained 3 epochs. Muon on conv filters (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov); SGD for biases and head (lr 0.053 / 0.67, momentum 0.85). Label smoothing 0.2, flip + translate 2, wd 2e-6 x batch, TTA level 2. 94.01% mean (n=200) in 2.59 s on a 400 W A100.
findings.relevance: Starting constants for the one decisive Muon check (H4.2.1). It also shows that a record recipe at ~8 epochs uses batch 2000, which supports testing larger batches given that E015 found the regime sample-limited.

findings.claim: The 24/28/32 progressive resize gave ~7.6% (1.98 -> 1.828 s) on top of an already-optimized base (whitened front end, compact 3-stage net, orthogonalized momentum + EMA-Lookahead, CUDA graphs, fused optimizer). Other legitimate gains came from schedule-length tuning (10.5 -> 9.0-9.75 epochs) and hyperparameter tuning. Precomputing data augmentation off the clock, host lottery and thermal cooldown were rejected as specification gaming (~15% cosmetic gain).
findings.relevance: Resize only pays well once per-step overhead is gone, which matches the 24px-curriculum finding. It is also a compliance warning: any augmentation precompute must stay in timed prepare/train, never in build.

findings.claim: Averaging checkpoints along the trajectory cut GPU-hours to reach the target by ~12% across the AlgoPerf suite. It works best combined with LR annealing and can replace the last phase of LR decay.
findings.relevance: General support for an LR floor plus a short averaging tail instead of decaying to zero. That is the H4.5.1 design, and it matches Fable's choice (5% floor plus an EMA tail).

findings.claim: A critical-damping momentum schedule (mu = 1 - 2*sqrt(lr)) reached 90% on CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 2.34x faster than constant 0.9, at a 0.46 pp final-accuracy cost. On CIFAR-100 the accuracy cost grew to 1.7 pp, leaving only a 1.14x gain at matched accuracy.
findings.relevance: Weak evidence that momentum-schedule and optimizer tricks tuned on CIFAR-10 shrink on CIFAR-100. It agrees with the low prior on Muon (H4.2) and argues for testing momentum changes carefully.

findings.claim: The only result the organizers publish is the ResNet9-style baseline (40 epochs, width 64): 75.36% (trials 75.56/75.16) in 59.30 s on an A100, with 0.117 s inference. Official judging uses 40 trials on an A100 80GB PCIe. No other leaderboard entries are public. The futurebiohackers PR reported 75.29% in 8.11 s on an A100-SXM4 (400 W) and noted that the official PCIe card (300 W) will likely be slower; that PR page now returns 404.
findings.relevance: E023 (6.65 s) already beats every public CIFAR-100 number found. The 300 W PCIe card is power-limited, so FLOP-bound gains may carry over differently from overhead-bound ones. Accuracy margins should keep the 0.753 safety buffer given ~0.3-0.4 pp run-to-run nondeterminism.
